target_customer: Smartphone users who want data, calls and texts without a carrier contract
problem: Mobile connectivity depends on carriers. Volk Fi proposed a phone, the Volk One, where each phone relays a distributed network so service works without a carrier SIM.
business_model: Phone hardware sale plus data allowance and overage at $1 per GB (per Notebookcheck)

founders.name: Greg Hazel
founders.background_notes: YC page gives no background. A search summary of CB Insights mentions other people and a prior BitTorrent role, but I did not open that page so none are recorded.

technical_complexity.rationale: A device that forms a distributed carrier like network, plus phone hardware and a Snapdragon 845 class design, is a hardware, networking and regulatory challenge for a tiny team.

defensibility.rationale: Any moat depended on network density that required many users; no evidence of patents or spectrum rights was found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No evidence of a carrier response was found.

market_need_then: Consumers disliked carrier pricing, but no data on demand for Volk One was found; the phone was announced with unknown price and shipping not before December 2019 per Notebookcheck.

branding.domain_note: Used volkfi.com. Fetch failed with a DNS error in 2026-11.

identity.logo: Rounded bold lettering for VolkFi and Volk1 per a design agency page
identity.visual_style: Rounded bold type with a gradient treatment on the wordmark per the agency's description

branding.community_and_virality: Phone announcement covered by Notebookcheck on 2019-03-21 and listed on Product Hunt as Volk One

brand_strength.rationale: Some tech press for the Volk One reveal and a design agency identity, but no evidence of continued community.

outcome_analysis: Volk Wireless joined YC Winter 2019 and drew press in March 2019 for the Volk One phone that promised carrier free service through a distributed network. Only a 150 thousand dollar seed was found and the YC directory lists the company inactive. No shipping, shutdown or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public. The failure factors are a low confidence inference from the hardware and network difficulty and the lack of later funding.
notes: The $150K seed rests on CB Insights and Startup Intros (both aggregators; dates 2019-03-19 and 2019-03-01). Founded year unknown. Competitors: Notebookcheck names none, and the dated fixed wireless results did not concern phones, so none listed. Co-founders named in a search summary of CB Insights were not confirmed by an opened source. Website did not resolve.
